task: Forward the configured max_output_tokens as max_tokens for Claude models on the LiteLLM-proxy path behind a kill switch, log the effective output-token limit per client build, and finalize plus WARN on text-only max_tokens truncation in the agent and supervisor event adapter (EPMCDME-15787).

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: LiteLLM chat client factory (enterprise/litellm/llm_factory.py: _resolve_max_output_tokens, _build_chat_model_base_args, _log_output_limit), LangGraph event adapter (agent and supervisor update paths, _finalize_truncated_text, module-level get_truncation_indicator), LangGraphAgent truncation helper (now delegates), Config (LLM_PROXY_FORWARD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS kill switch)

requirements_clarity.label: L
requirements_clarity.gaps: AC5 did not say whether truncation should be a hard error, a response flag or a log-only signal. The team chose B-lite (finalize the thought and WARN) and deferred response-level exposure to EPMCDME-14145. How widely to forward the limit was not settled up front: code review CR-002 narrowed forwarding to Claude-only, which meant reworking the spec and code. AC2-AC4 can only be checked after deployment.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Root cause depended on LiteLLM internals (model-map lookup, DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_CHAT_MAX_TOKENS=4096, thinking budget+4096) and had to be verified on two versions (1.84.0 local, 1.99.2 locked). Every proxied Claude request now sends an explicit max_tokens: a catalog value above the provider cap now returns 400 instead of being silently capped, and Bedrock reserves TPM quota at 128k per request. Forwarding to non-Anthropic providers turned out to be risky (prompt + max_tokens over the context window, Azure TPM), found in review. Edge case found in review: a truncated tool call whose arguments were cut mid-JSON (invalid_tool_calls) must still raise. The adapter changes run on every agent and supervisor stream.
technical_risk.mitigation: LLM_PROXY_FORWARD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS kill switch (rollback without redeploy). Positive-int guard that rejects bool and non-int values. Existing features.max_tokens=False opt-out kept. Claude-only scope. Agent outcomes unchanged (finalize plus WARN only). Parameterized tests over values and log sources. Full suite with merge-base failure classification (0 regressions).

key_reasoning.reason: Three components were touched: the LiteLLM chat client factory, the LangGraph event adapter (agent and supervisor branches) with the agent's truncation helper, and Config. On its own that is M (2-3 components, clear pattern). It is bumped to L because the factory is the shared client builder behind every proxied LLM call. Same score as the initial estimate.

Up from the initial M. The ACs were explicit, but key decisions were open: how to handle truncation (hard error vs response flag vs B-lite), how far to forward the limit, and what to defer to EPMCDME-14145. A product-owner decision during code review (CR-002, Claude-only) changed both the spec and the code. Two review rounds and four commits reflect that rework.

Up from the initial M. A native-factory precedent exists, but proving the root cause meant tracing LiteLLM default resolution on two versions. The behavior change hits every proxied Claude request and has provider-specific failure modes (400s, Bedrock TPM reservation). Review found two real risks: forwarding to non-Claude providers, and truncated invalid_tool_calls. The kill switch and a rollback plan were needed, which fits L. Not XL: rollback is a config flip and outcomes are unchanged.
